2181.summary: The class explores the concept of the Trinity as a mystery in Christianity, arguing that it is used as a crutch to avoid deeper biblical understanding. It emphasizes the importance of understanding God's character and relationship with Christ through Scripture, aiming to show that Christadelphian beliefs make more sense and align better with biblical teachings.

2182.summary: The class explores how God uses representatives, like angels, to bear His name and character, emphasizing that God's name signifies His attributes. It examines passages like Exodus 34 and Genesis 18 to show how angels can be called by God's name, acting on His behalf and representing Him.

2183.summary: The class explores Jesus as a mediator and representative of God, emphasizing his role in manifesting God's character and actions. It contrasts the concept of the Trinity with God manifestation, highlighting Jesus' humanity and his perfect representation of God's will.

2184.summary: The class explores the concept of being united with Christ, emphasizing the difference between being called by God's name and actually possessing it. It highlights Jesus' resurrection and receiving God's name, paralleling this with the hope of believers' resurrection and transformation into Christ's character.

2185.summary: The class discusses the true meaning of the atonement, contrasting mainstream Christian views with biblical teachings. It emphasizes that Jesus did not die as a substitute but to declare God's righteousness and love, encouraging followers to manifest God's glory through their actions and crucify their flesh daily.
